chunks: Ibn Faḍḍāl, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Everyone who kills something, small or great, after doing so intentionally, then retaliation is upon him.

key_terms.الْقَوَدُ: retaliation; qisas, the legal requital for intentional killing
key_terms.شَيْئًا: a thing; here indicating any victim without distinction in the wording
key_terms.صَغِيرًا: small; indicating lesser size or status in the general expression
key_terms.قَتَلَ: killed; committed the act of killing
key_terms.كَبِيرًا: great; indicating larger size or status in the general expression
key_terms.يَتَعَمَّدَ: acts intentionally; does so deliberately and with purpose

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intentional killing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that intentional killing incurs qisas, without distinction between what is small or great. Its significance is in affirming deliberate intent as the basis for legal retaliation in cases of unlawful killing.
